title: Substitute silicon channel with beta-Ga2O3 ultrawide-gap access transistor
idea: Substitute the crystalline-Si access channel with a 4-6 nm beta-Ga2O3 (Eg 4.8 eV) gate-all-around channel built as a tier over the CMOS periphery and crystallized by local anneal. Its intrinsic carrier density is ~1e-22 that of Si, and because it contains no indium it avoids the indium supply that IGZO depends on.
why: Leakage tail/refresh: off-current below 1e-20 A per cell stretches retention from 64 ms to >100 s, cutting refresh energy and bandwidth loss by >99%. It goes beyond the IGZO prior work with a wider gap and no indium.

title: Swap thermionic switching for heterojunction tunnel-FET access device
idea: Substitute the MOSFET's thermionic barrier with band-to-band tunneling: a p+ SiGe source on the bitline side, an intrinsic Si channel and a lightly doped n storage side. The device is asymmetric (it tunnels only when the wordline is high) and sub-60 mV/dec, and the lightly doped storage side suppresses ambipolar leakage.
why: Voltage floor + leakage: the steep slope lets VPP drop from ~3 V to ~1.5 V (~4x lower wordline CV^2 energy) while keeping fA-class off-current, so refresh activation energy falls too.

title: Replace semiconductor switch with non-touching tunneling-gap NEMS relay
idea: Substitute the channel with a vacuum-gap nanomechanical beam. When the wordline pulls it in, it stops ~1 nm from the storage electrode on an oxide standoff, so charge moves by electron tunneling and never by metal contact. When released (gap >5 nm), the only off-current is vacuum tunneling, effectively zero.
why: Leakage/refresh: off-leakage below an attoampere leaves retention limited only by the capacitor dielectric (hours). Because the contacts never touch, there is no wear (target >1e15 cycles).

title: Substitute biased well with buried fixed-charge Al2O3 back-gate
idea: Substitute the charge-pumped negative body bias (VBB) with a 3-5 nm ALD Al2O3/SiO2 liner on the back side of each buried or vertical channel. Its built-in negative fixed charge (~-5e12 cm^-2) permanently depletes the body near the storage junction and raises off-state Vt by ~150-250 mV at zero standby power.
why: Leakage + periphery: ~10-30x lower subthreshold leakage for tail cells, and the VBB pump and its idle power (part of the 16-33% idle budget) go away.

title: Move drain high-field region into wide-gap heterojunction contact
idea: Substitute the n+ Si storage-node junction with a heterojunction: the gate-drain overlap and storage contact are n+ ZnO or TiO2 (Eg ~3.3 eV) grown on the Si channel. The conduction bands align so electrons pass, while a ~2-3 eV valence offset blocks holes. The high-field region where GIDL and SRH generation occur now sits in a material with ~1e-20 lower intrinsic carrier density.
why: Leakage tail (GIDL + junction): targets a 10-100x drop in the <=13 fA tail, extending tREF by 10x or more and cutting refresh energy ~90%.

title: Borrow power-MOSFET field plate to flatten storage-node field
idea: Substitute the bare gate-drain overlap with a grounded buried field plate, as used in power LDMOS: a thin TiN shield in the isolation next to the storage contact, tied to ground. It spreads the lateral field so the peak field at the overlap drops ~20-30%.
why: GIDL is exponential in peak field, so tail cells see ~10x less GIDL and the wordline can be biased more negative without a GIDL penalty: 4-8x longer refresh interval.

title: Replace amorphous oxide liners with epitaxial CaF2 crystalline insulator
idea: Substitute the amorphous SiO2/SiN gate insulator and isolation liner around the access channel with epitaxial CaF2 (0.6% lattice mismatch to Si) grown by MBE on Si {111} facets. A crystalline insulator has orders of magnitude fewer border traps than an amorphous oxide.
why: Variable retention time (VRT) and random telegraph noise come from border and oxide traps; removing them shrinks the retention tail so refresh is set by the bulk distribution: 2-4x longer tREF.

title: Substitute electrical wordline with optical wordline and photoconductive access
idea: Substitute the metal wordline and gate with one silicon-nitride waveguide per row feeding a wide-gap (AlGaN or diamond) photoconductive switch at each cell. A pulse from an on-chip micro-LED makes the switch conduct; in the dark it is an insulator with attoampere-scale leakage.
why: Removes the 3 V wordline pump and the wordline RC delay and gives near-zero dark leakage (refresh-free retention); no wordline coupling for row hammer. Switching speed and persistent photoconductivity are the risk.

title: Swap electrostatic gating for piezoelectronic pressure-driven insulator-metal switch
idea: Substitute the gate field with mechanical pressure: a thin AlScN piezo actuator squeezes a pressure-sensitive insulator-metal transition layer (SmSe-type) between storage node and bitline. Under GPa-scale stress its resistance drops ~1e4-1e6; relaxed, it is a bandgap insulator.
why: Steep ~0.3 V switching breaks the wordline voltage floor, and the off state is a true insulator rather than a weakly-off transistor: ~10x wordline energy and long retention claimed.

title: Insert NbO2 threshold switch to make access turn-on abrupt
idea: Substitute the plain access FET with a hyper-FET: a 10 nm NbO2 layer in series with the bitline-side source. NbO2's insulator-metal transition is at ~800 C, so it is stable at 85 C operation, and the layer snaps on abruptly once current flows, giving an effective sub-60 mV/dec turn-on. That lets the FET's Vt rise ~200 mV at the same wordline swing.
why: ~100x lower off-leakage from the higher Vt without raising VPP: longer refresh interval or a lower wordline voltage.

title: Substitute linear gate dielectric with antiferroelectric ZrO2 steep-switch stack
idea: Substitute the HfO2/SiO2 gate stack with antiferroelectric ZrO2. Its field-induced AFE-to-FE transition gives a transient negative-capacitance boost at turn-on, then relaxes fully to zero polarization at zero field: no remanence and none of the wake-up or fatigue of ferroelectric gates.
why: Sub-60 mV/dec turn-on allows a higher Vt and lower VPP: target ~10x lower leakage or ~1 V less wordline, without ferroelectric endurance limits.

title: Replace transistor with two-terminal punch-through selector: cross-point DRAM
idea: Substitute the 3-terminal access transistor with a 2-terminal n+/p-/n+ punch-through (or back-to-back Schottky) selector stacked on an MIM capacitor at every wordline/bitline crossing (1S1C). Idle lines sit at mid-level so each selector sees near-zero bias, and writes use V/2 half-select.
why: A stackable 4F^2 cross-point cell with no lateral transistor (the 3D DRAM blocker): denser per layer, with many layers. Retention needs a selector nonlinearity of >1e9 between V and V/2.

title: Invert strain engineering: heavy-valley transport suppresses source-drain tunneling
idea: Substitute mobility-boosting strain with the opposite: uniaxial compressive stress along a <100> channel fills the Si valleys whose heavy longitudinal mass (0.92 m0) points along transport. Direct source-to-drain tunneling at 6-8 nm gate length then falls exponentially, while on-current drops only ~2x.
why: Lets the access transistor shrink below ~10 nm gate length without a tunneling-leakage floor: ~10-100x lower direct-tunneling leakage, which helps both density and refresh.

title: Substitute oxygen-precipitate gettering with implanted nanocavity gettering layer
idea: Substitute intrinsic oxygen-precipitate gettering with a buried band of nanocavities 1-2 um under the cell array, made by light-ion implant and anneal. Cavity walls bind Fe, Cu and Ni far more strongly than precipitates do, pulling the deep-level metal centers that create tail cells away from the storage junctions.
why: A few defect-bearing junctions dominate the retention tail; cleaning them pulls it toward the main distribution (2-4x tREF) and relaxes wafer-quality needs, so less depends on Cz quartz crucibles.

title: Trim each leaky cell's Vt via access-gate charge trap
idea: Substitute worst-case refresh with per-cell repair. The access gate stack includes a thin nitride trap layer; after retention test, the ppm of tail cells are programmed by hot-carrier injection at their bitline-side edge (bitline biased as drain). That raises their source-barrier Vt by ~150-200 mV without adding storage-side GIDL, and the trapped charge holds for years, as in SONOS.
why: The <=13 fA tail sets tREF for every cell; trimming it lets the chip refresh at the median cell's rate: 4-10x fewer refreshes and 10-20% of bandwidth recovered.

title: Substitute periodic refresh with static Esaki tunnel-diode latch per cell
idea: Substitute capacitor decay plus refresh with a bistable hold: two series interband (Esaki) tunnel diodes at the storage node form a negative-differential-resistance latch with two stable voltages. A tiny valley current (target ~pA) holds the state continuously, and the access transistor still reads and writes it.
why: Removes refresh entirely (16-33% of idle power, 10-20% of bandwidth) in exchange for a static current; viable if the valley current is engineered below ~10 pA per cell.

title: Substitute row-level refresh with mat-local segmented refresh for weak cells
idea: Substitute full-row (8 KB) refresh with sub-row refresh: hierarchical wordlines already have per-mat local drivers, so add a per-mat enable. Only the ~512-cell mats that hold profiled weak cells get the fast refresh rate; the rest of the row runs at a 4-8x longer interval.
why: Weak cells are sparse, so refreshing only their mats cuts tail refresh energy 16-64x versus row-granular retention-aware refresh, for a few gates per mat.

title: Substitute hard-switched refresh with LC resonant charge recovery
idea: Substitute CV^2-dissipating drivers with adiabatic resonant drive: an inductor on the package or interposer resonates with wordline and bitline capacitance. Two subarrays refresh in antiphase, so energy swings back and forth between them instead of burning in drivers.
why: Refresh energy (~46 fJ/bit) and voltage floor: recovers ~50-70% of refresh-burst CV^2. Refresh is periodic and schedulable, which suits resonant drive.

title: Substitute fixed sense reference with co-decaying reference cells
idea: Substitute the static VDD/2 bitline reference with reference cells in each row, written to half charge whenever the row is written. They leak through identical access transistors, so the sense threshold sags with the '1' cells instead of staying fixed.
why: Sense margin decays more slowly: 2-3x longer refresh interval for ~1% array area, with refresh energy and bandwidth loss cut proportionally.

title: Substitute raw data storage with leakage-minimizing per-row polarity coding
idea: Substitute raw data with a per-row inversion flag chosen at write time so most cells sit in their discharged, non-leaking state (true-cell/anti-cell layout included). The row's charged-cell count is stored, and rows with few charged cells are refreshed at a relaxed rate.
why: On average halves the number of cells exposed to leakage; with ECC margin, 1.5-2x less refresh from a pure controller/DRAM-logic change.

title: Substitute per-word SECDED with row-wide LDPC in sense stripe
idea: Substitute 64-bit Hamming with a 4 KB-row LDPC code: parity sits in spare columns and the decoder in the sense-amp stripe. Tail-cell retention failures become correctable erasures, so tREFI can be set at a ~1e-5 raw bit error rate instead of zero failures.
why: 8-16x longer refresh interval (refresh energy and the 10-20% bandwidth loss recovered) for ~6% parity overhead.

title: Substitute 85 C air-cooled DIMMs with 35 C cold plates
idea: Substitute air cooling with direct liquid cold plates holding DIMMs and HBM at ~35 C, plus a new JEDEC 'cool-tier' mode register that certifies temperature-scaled refresh (leakage halves every ~8-10 C).
why: Running 50 C cooler gives ~16-32x retention; refresh drops at least 8x, recovering most of the 10-20% bandwidth and the 16-33% idle-power share of refresh.

title: Substitute scrapping retention-fail dies with retention-binned memory SKUs
idea: Substitute pass/fail retention screening with binning. Dies that fail 64 ms at 85 C are sold with an SPD flag for 32 ms refresh or for cooled racks; long-retention dies sell at a premium into low-power edge and mobile.
why: Raises usable bit supply 3-8% from existing wafers with zero capital, and turns retention into a priced feature.

title: Substitute hydrogen forming gas with deuterium-in-nitrogen anneal
idea: Substitute the H2/N2 (or argon-diluted) forming-gas anneal with high-pressure D2 in N2 after BEOL. Si-D bonds at access-transistor interfaces resist field- and hot-carrier-driven depassivation ~10x better (kinetic isotope effect), so fewer traps form over the part's life. No rare gas is used at any step.
why: Attacks variable retention time and aging of the leakage tail: a tighter tail over life allows 1.5-3x more refresh margin and less guardband.

title: Substitute helium cryogenics with liquid-nitrogen-immersed DRAM tier
idea: Substitute any helium cryostat with 77 K liquid-nitrogen immersion for a pooled-memory sled; the nitrogen comes from air separation, with no helium or neon. At 77 K subthreshold and junction leakage fall more than 1e6x and retention reaches hours, so the access transistor can use a lower Vt and a ~1.5 V wordline.
why: Refresh essentially disappears, wordline energy drops ~4x and wire resistance ~5x; cryocooler energy is traded for density and refresh savings in a disaggregated pool.

title: Substitute argon-purged Cz crystal with hydrogen-ambient crucible-free silicon
idea: Substitute argon-purged Czochralski pulling in quartz crucibles with electromagnetic cold-crucible casting in a hydrogen/nitrogen ambient for the substrate. The access transistors live in a 3-5 um low-oxygen epitaxial layer grown by H2-carrier CVD, with nitrogen co-doping for gettering.
why: Removes the argon and Spruce Pine quartz chokepoints, and low-oxygen epi has fewer generation centers, so the leakage tail improves rather than worsens.

title: Substitute excimer and EUV lithography with nanoimprint for wordline trenches
idea: Substitute ArF scanners (argon/neon gas laser) and EUV (CO2 drive laser with helium in its gas mix) with UV-LED-cured nanoimprint from e-beam-written masters for the buried-wordline and active layers. The periodic DRAM array suits imprint, which reproduces the master's ~1 nm line-edge roughness.
why: Lower line-edge roughness gives tighter access-transistor Vt and leakage spread (sigma-Vt down ~30%), shrinking the tail that sets refresh, while cutting litho capex and rare-gas use.

title: Substitute sputtered TiN/W wordline with ALD molybdenum nitride gradient
idea: Substitute the argon-sputtered TiN liner and CVD tungsten fill with thermal ALD Mo (MoO2Cl2 + H2, N2 purge). NH3 pulses near the trench top make the MoNx there lower in work function than the deep channel region, keeping Vt high while lowering the gate-drain field at the storage overlap.
why: The graded work function cuts GIDL ~5-10x without losing off-state Vt, and removes the tungsten (China ~80%) and argon-sputter dependence.

title: Substitute plasma etching of access pillars with TMAH crystallographic etch
idea: Substitute argon/helium-diluted plasma etch of fins and pillars with a hard-masked TMAH wet etch that stops on {111} planes. The channel sidewalls come out atomically flat and damage-free, with tightly controlled width.
why: Plasma damage and sidewall roughness create interface traps and Vt scatter; damage-free {111} sidewalls aim for ~3-5x lower interface-trap density, shrinking the leakage tail and VRT.

title: Substitute helium backside cooling with hydrogen for cryogenic implants
idea: Substitute the helium backside gas in the implanter chuck with low-pressure H2, which conducts heat even better than helium, to hold wafers at -100 C during storage-node junction implants. The cold implant fully amorphizes the region, which then regrows by solid-phase epitaxy without end-of-range dislocation loops.
why: End-of-range defects sit inside the storage-junction depletion region and drive SRH junction leakage; removing them cuts tail leakage ~3-10x.

title: Substitute xenon flash and excimer anneals with microwave activation
idea: Substitute xenon flash-lamp and excimer-laser anneals (both rare-gas tools) with 5.8 GHz microwave annealing below 500 C. The microwaves couple to implant damage and dopants, activating and healing them without diffusing the graded storage-junction profile.
why: Keeps a soft, graded junction that lowers BTBT/GIDL while repairing damage-related generation centers: target 2-5x lower junction leakage from a gas-free tool.

title: Substitute beamline implant with self-assembled monolayer doping on 3D channels
idea: Substitute ion implantation (whose plasma flood guns run on argon or xenon) with monolayer doping. Phosphorus- or boron-bearing molecules self-assemble on exposed Si sidewalls from solution, are capped with oxide, and are driven in by semiconductor diode-laser spike heating, forming a conformal, damage-free, sub-5 nm junction even on the lateral channels of 3D DRAM tiers.
why: No implant damage, which removes a main source of tail-leakage traps, and conformal doping of stacked lateral transistors, a 3D DRAM blocker.

title: Substitute litho-defined pillars with self-ordered anodic alumina templates
idea: Substitute lithography for the vertical-channel array with anodized aluminum: self-ordered hexagonal pores ~15-25 nm wide, guided by a shallow imprinted pre-pattern. Vertical channels are grown inside the pores by selective H2-carrier epitaxy or ALD, and the alumina stays as the host for the gate dielectric.
why: The wet electrochemistry needs no rare gas and no EUV/DUV, and pore diameter is fixed by anodization voltage, tightening channel width and leakage spread while slashing capex.

title: Substitute sputtered IGZO with N2-curtain spatial-ALD gallium-tin oxide
idea: Substitute argon/oxygen-sputtered IGZO with amorphous Ga-Sn-O deposited by atmospheric-pressure spatial ALD, in which nitrogen gas curtains rather than argon separate the precursor zones. The result is an indium-free wide-gap channel with angstrom thickness control at high throughput.
why: Indium-free oxide-semiconductor access devices (~1e-19 A/um off-current class) made without rare gases or vacuum tools: a cheaper BEOL tier for refresh-light gain cells.

title: Substitute silicon channel with sulfurized MoS2 grown in H2S/N2
idea: Substitute Si with a bilayer MoS2 access channel made by ALD of MoO3 and conversion in H2S/N2 at ~600 C in a resistive furnace (no argon carrier), then encapsulated in thermal-ALD Al2O3. The ~1.3 nm body has no dangling-bond surface generation sites and near-ideal electrostatics.
why: The atomically thin body and 1.6-1.8 eV gap suppress subthreshold and short-channel tunneling leakage: target <1 aA per cell, with gate length down to ~5 nm for 3D stacking.

title: Substitute amorphous oxides with MBE-grown BaSnO3 perovskite channel
idea: Substitute amorphous oxide channels with La-doped BaSnO3 grown by MBE on a SrTiO3 buffer on Si (ultra-high vacuum, ozone oxidant, no carrier or sputter gas). It is a 3.1 eV-gap perovskite with film mobility above 100 cm^2/Vs, so on-current and off-leakage stop trading against each other.
why: At least 5x the on-current of IGZO at similar sub-aA leakage: shorter write times and refresh-light cells without large transistors.

title: Substitute mask lithography with solid-state DUV interference patterning
idea: Substitute neon-buffered excimer scanners with a frequency-quintupled solid-state laser (213 nm) in a two- or four-beam interference tool that prints the periodic wordline and active gratings without a mask; cut layers are done by imprint.
why: Interference gratings have near-zero CD variation and line-edge roughness, tightening access-transistor leakage spread, and remove the neon/EUV dependence at far below scanner cost.

title: Substitute plasma channel thinning with thermal atomic-layer etching
idea: Substitute argon-ion or plasma recess of ultrathin channels with thermal atomic-layer etching (oxidation/fluorination plus ligand-exchange cycles, N2 purged). It removes ~0.1 nm per cycle with no ion damage and sets channel body thickness to within one monolayer.
why: Body-thickness variation is a leading source of Vt scatter in thin channels; monolayer control halves sigma-Vt and shrinks the leakage tail ~10x.

title: Substitute hydrogen-passivated oxide channels with HF-vapor fluorine passivation
idea: Substitute hydrogen, a shallow donor and instability source in oxide semiconductors, with fluorine: oxide-channel access transistors are annealed in anhydrous HF vapor diluted in N2 instead of CF4/Ar plasma. The fluorine fills oxygen vacancies and replaces mobile hydrogen.
why: Fewer subgap states and no hydrogen drift give low, stable off-current (~10x less drift-induced leakage), allowing longer refresh intervals for oxide-channel cells.

title: Substitute hours-long retention bakes with infrared photo-stimulated screening
idea: Substitute multi-hour hot-bake retention tests with sub-bandgap (~1.3-1.6 um) LED illumination at wafer sort. The light photo-ionizes the deep traps behind tail cells and speeds up only defect-assisted leakage, so a scan of a few seconds yields retention maps per row and per mat.
why: A cheap, gas-free test step that makes retention-aware refresh and binning practical at volume: more usable supply and 4-8x refresh cuts.

title: Substitute blanket refresh with compiler-declared short-lifetime no-refresh zones
idea: Substitute uniform refresh with lifetime-aware refresh. An AI compiler places activations, gradients and KV-cache blocks that live shorter than the guaranteed retention window in banks flagged 'no-refresh', and the controller refreshes a bank only when its oldest live write exceeds that window. No new process or tool is needed, so no gases.
why: Much of accelerator DRAM holds data that lives under 10 ms; skipping its refresh cuts refresh energy ~50-80% in those banks and recovers bandwidth.

title: Substitute explicit refresh with weight-streaming reads that restore rows
idea: Substitute refresh commands for LLM weight regions with read-restore. During decode every weight row is activated once per token (~20-50 ms), and each activation fully restores its charge, so the controller tracks how often each row is read and suppresses refresh while serving. This is controller logic only, with no fab step.
why: Weights fill most HBM capacity in inference, so refresh there is pure waste: ~10% of bandwidth and refresh energy recovered.

title: Substitute VDD/2 idle bitline with trimmed leakage-balance parking voltage
idea: Substitute the fixed VDD/2 standby bitline level with a parking voltage trimmed per subarray by an on-die DAC at test. It is set where channel leakage into the storage node offsets junction and GIDL leakage out of it for the weakest profiled cells.
why: Cuts the weakest cells' net leakage ~2-5x, extending the tail-limited refresh interval with existing devices and no new process step (so no rare gases).

title: Substitute static cell plate with idle-lowered plate voltage
idea: Substitute the constant cell-plate voltage with one that drops ~0.2-0.3 V while a bank is idle. That couples every floating storage node down and shrinks the storage-to-gate field that drives GIDL on '1' cells; the plate returns before activation, and the negative wordline tracks it to keep '0' cells off.
why: GIDL-dominated tail leakage drops ~3-5x, lengthening the self-refresh interval accordingly; a circuit-only change needing no gas-consuming process step.

title: Substitute oxide isolation with sacrificial-carbon air gaps near passing gates
idea: Substitute the dielectric between passing (neighbor) wordlines and the storage-node junction with an air gap: amorphous carbon is deposited from C2H2/H2 with no argon or helium dilution, then burned out through a porous cap in O2.
why: Passing-gate coupling modulates storage-junction leakage whenever neighbors switch; an air gap (k ~1) cuts that coupling ~3x, reducing activity-dependent leakage and row-hammer-like retention loss.

title: Substitute gas-exposed access modules with rare-gas-free certified process kit
idea: Substitute ad hoc process choices with a U.S. DPA/CHIPS-funded 'noble-gas-free access module': D2 anneal, thermal-ALD Mo gates, imprint/interference patterning and microwave activation, qualified as a drop-in kit any U.S. memory or foundry line can license, with shared reliability data on leakage tails.
why: Shields U.S. DRAM capacity from Qatar helium and neon supply shocks, lowers entry capital for new memory fabs, and shortens qualification by 1-2 years.
